title: useDispatch
description: Learn how to dispatch actions to the Redux store.

data.text: **useDispatch** returns the Redux store's `dispatch` function. This is how components send actions to update the state. Without dispatch, your components couldn't change anything in the store.

When you dispatch an action, Redux passes it through the middleware chain and then to the reducer. The reducer returns a new state based on the action type. The flow goes: **Component** → **dispatch(action)** → **Middleware** → **Reducer** → **New State**.

cards.title: Direct dispatch({ type: ... })
cards.content: Quick and simple for one-off actions. Good for learning. Harder to test and reuse.

cards.title: Action Creators (Recommended)
cards.content: Functions that return actions. Reusable, testable, type-safe. Best practice for production apps.

data.title: Action Creators
Stable Reference
data.text: The dispatch function returned by useDispatch is stable across renders. Unlike useSelector, storing it in a variable won't cause re-renders unless you use it in a dependency array.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: useDispatch returns the store's dispatch function for sending actions
Dispatch an action to trigger state updates through the reducer
Always use action creators for reusable, testable actions
Dispatch is stable across renders - store without causing re-renders
Use typed dispatch (AppDispatch) in TypeScript projects
data.takeaway: useDispatch is how React components communicate with the Redux store to update application state.
